title: Geospatial diversity workflows
text: Forest dynamics plots (ForestGEO / CTFS) map every stem local metres repeat census every five years (Condit 1998; Anderson-Teixeira et al. 2015). tidymapr handles spatial steps tidydiversity census summaries: tidydiversity::stems_as_trees() picks main stem per tree. [stems_quadrat()] assigns 20 m x 20 m quadrats gx / gy. tidydiversity::stems_abundance() tidydiversity::stems_basal_area() summarise counts basal area (pi/4 * dbh^2). tidydiversity::stems_size_class() bins DBH. tidydiversity::stems_demography() estimates mortality, recruitment growth two censuses. [stems_habitat()] joins quadrat topography habitat, [stems_neighbours()] counts neighbours within radius [stems_habitat_test()] runs torus-translation habitat test. tidydiversity::stems_as_community() feeds tidydiversity::div_hill() friends. [plot_topo()] maps stems hillshade contours.

what: Partial-effect and surface plots (Moses et al. 2021)
title: Geospatial diversity workflows
text: Mt Wilhelm litter-ant analysis Moses et al. (2021, doi:10.1111/btp.12914) fitted Poisson negative-binomial GLMs richness abundance elevation litter depth, used visreg (visreg2d) interaction surface hand-converted result ggplot. tidydiversity replaces jump tidydiversity::model_count(), tidydiversity::plot_partial() tidydiversity::plot_surface() one tidy workflow (visreg, plotmo aods3).
code: ants <- png_ants |>   dplyr::group_by(site, elevation) |>   dplyr::summarise(richness = dplyr::n_distinct(species), .groups = "drop") set.seed(1) ants$litter <- 1 + ants$elevation / 2000 + stats::rnorm(nrow(ants), 0, 0.25) fit <- model_count(   ants, richness ~ elevation * litter, family = "poisson" ) plot_partial(fit, elevation, residuals = TRUE) +   ggplot2::labs(title = "Partial effect of elevation on richness") plot_surface(fit, elevation, litter) +   ggplot2::labs(     title = "Elevation x litter surface",     subtitle = "Pattern after Moses et al. 2021; illustrative litter values"   )

title: Automatic publication maps that explain their choices — geo_automap
text: geo_automap() draws finished map one call, spirit GeoSpaX's AutoMap. looks data chooses, reason choice: projection: Equal Earth world-wide data (true areas), Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred data continents large regions, local UTM zone study areas (distances metres); symbology, following conventions GeoSpaX's AutoMap, ArcGIS QGIS: numbers points, lines polygons get graduated colours classes (classed legend, never continuous ramp). method follows shape data: equal intervals roughly symmetric (|skew| < 0.5), natural breaks (Jenks) skewed, quantiles heavy-tailed (|skew| >= 2); 5 classes 30 features, fewer small samples; colour ramp follows field's meaning: blues water rain, greens vegetation, viridis elevation, slope predictions, diverging ramp values cross zero, yellow-orange-red otherwise; small whole-number counts points get proportional circles; categories get qualitative Okabe-Ito colours; features without value get single symbol; continuous surfaces (raster x, background DEM sites) get stretched colour ramp gradient legend, place gradient legend used; basemap: none world regional maps background surface; topographic tiles study areas, muted context legend (coastline offline); furniture: graticule world outline world maps; scale bar north arrow regional local maps, corners chosen avoid data. Everything can overridden arguments, result normal ggplot can keep editing. geo_automap_explain() returns decisions table, ready methods section.
